source_text: Sin autem dixeris per peccatum Adae naturalem factam esse iniquitatem duasque accidisse mortes, unam aeternam, alteram temporalem, per Christi autem gratiam unam interim auferri a persona, non a natura, id est perpetuam, temporalem vero remanere, Apostolus convincitur falsitatis, qui dixit multo magis profuisse gratiam quam nocuisse peccatum [n137] ; Apostolus autem argui non potest, tu igitur iure reprobaris.
pass_a_gloss: But if you shall have said that through Adam's sin iniquity was made natural and two deaths happened, one eternal, the other temporal, but through the grace of Christ one is meanwhile taken away from the person, not from nature, that is the perpetual, but the temporal remains, the Apostle is convicted of falsehood, who said that grace helped much more than sin harmed; but the Apostle cannot be accused, you therefore are rightly rejected.

lemmas.lexica: LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'
LS mors; Blaise temporal vs eternal death in Rom 5

pass_b_english: But if you say that through Adam’s sin wickedness became natural and two deaths arose, one eternal and the other temporal, while through Christ’s grace only one—the everlasting death—is removed for the present from the person, not from nature, and temporal death remains, then the apostle is convicted of falsehood. For he said that grace helped much more than sin harmed (Romans 5:15). But the apostle cannot be accused. You, therefore, are rightly rejected.

choices.why: Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
